items.content: NEVER spend the user's money. No metered API call, no billed CLI invocation (including `claude -p` / headless Claude Code), no paid service — not to build a feature, not to test one, and never to inspect a response shape. If a design needs a paid call, quote the price BEFORE writing the code, and never present a paid option in a choice list without its cost attached: an option chosen without its price is not informed consent. Never put a billed call on a timer, hook, or any unattended path — that is a standing charge, not a feature. When a paid path must be removed, DELETE it rather than gate it behind a flag; a switch that can be flipped is not a guarantee. The correct free substitute is almost always to prepare the work (file a self-contained request with everything needed) and let the reading happen inside the interactive session the user is already paying for.
items.why: Money leaves the account and does not come back, and an automated caller repeats the mistake while nobody is watching. Cost is invisible in a way bugs are not: nothing errors, nothing looks broken, and the only signal is a bill later. Incident: an agent-audit step was implemented as `claude -p` fired from a 5-minute scheduler and shipped switched ON. Three billed calls (~$0.29), one of them purely to look at a JSON envelope's shape, and cost instrumentation was only added after the first spend so most of it was never even recorded.
